Q1.e: All three reveal stages are keyed 'b'; in each, b is the longest, the only hedged/nuanced option, and the other two are extremes ('곧 채택', '이미 거절', '영원히 거절', '무시해도', '지금 바로 만들라'). A student can answer b,b,b with no reading of the email. Stage 2 b even pre-announces stage 3 ('이후에 대해서는 아직 아무 말이 없다'). Because the correct answer never changes, no revision of judgement is ever required, contradicting the format 'reveal-and-revise'.

Q2.e: Alternatives/hardCases say a tentative or 'polite refusal' reading of stage 1 and 3 is reasonable, but no option expresses it, so only b can be chosen. s2 checker: false rejections of valid promises: 'I'll send you the costs tomorrow', 'on Thursday', 'this Wednesday', 'soon' (w3 needs friday/by/before/deadline/this week); false acceptance 'Thank you. I'm sad about the budget, by the way.' ('by' matches).

Q4.e: Reveals on wrong options are informative (e.g. 'budget already fixed'). But the right option is not distinguished by evidence quotes, and reflect has no input.

themes: Distractors that are absurd or refuted by the text, plus the correct option being the longest/most hedged (e-04,e-05,e-06,e-07,e-10); e-10 is b,b,b in every stage

Write-step regex checks reject valid answers (can not, not coming, tomorrow, unclear, number words, 'three') and accept wrong ones (original text unchanged in e-02, concatenated originals in e-06, 'Yes... can't wait' in e-01, copy minus 'something' in e-08, 'example' as 'exam' in e-11)
Substring patterns without word boundaries (fri in friends, exam in example, test in latest)
Hints sometimes give the answer set (e-09 s2, e-12 s1, e-03 s1, e-08 s1 contradiction)
pickLine/omission in multi-choice give no diagnostic message; reflect prompts (e-04, e-10) have no response capture
Revise-judgement tasks (e-04, e-10) do not force an actual revision
Strength: transferable ideas in e-05 (register), e-11 (post hoc), e-09/e-03 (missing info); Korean instructions are natural overall
